## Audio File Preview — waveform + player (AP)

The other half of the **Media File Preview** row.

**The browser is the decoder** — the reading formats mount one native `<audio controls>`. But a sound file **has no picture**, so the visual handed to the shells is the amplitude envelope the extract pass read out of the bytes, drawn as a waveform.

### The envelope arrives already bounded

`fileViewModel` resamples it before this component sees it: **64 bars in a fitted cell, 256 in the reading formats**. This component only draws — it never sees an unbounded payload, which is what keeps a grid of audio files cheap.

### A file with no envelope still renders

An over-budget FLAC, a stream that would not re-read: the **duration and identity carry the cell**, and the waveform area falls back to the family glyph. Never a broken frame. This is the rule across the whole family — a file that is genuinely playable must not lose its card because one derived fact could not be computed.

### Related but different

The catalog ships `fields/audio` with `MiniPlayer`, `WaveformPlayer` and six siblings — a full **AudioField** for authored audio with likes, play counts and trim. That is for audio a card *owns*. This is for **any audio file in a realm**, with no card modelling it.


Projected into the four format shells by `FilePreviewStage`, which owns the loading, failure and staleness panes.
